acceptance: The page is published in the site docs and navigation, and the site build and documentation checks pass.
Every normative statement cites an existing source (an ADR, a validator rule or observed CLI behaviour); the PR body carries the source table.
Statements about CLI or MCP behaviour, such as default iterations and default validation mode, are verified by running the command, with output in the PR.
The scattered pages named in the description link to the new page, and the PR lists each page checked for contradiction.
Publication and licensing wording agrees with docs/tpc-licensing-analysis.md and DISCLAIMER.md and makes no claim to be legal advice.

The page states the subscale ranking decision as recorded: TPC-H and TPC-DS runs below scale factor 1 are unofficial subscale results that remain ranked; only non-standard runs are excluded from ranking.

Vendor terms on publishing benchmark results appear under 'Open questions' unless results-vendor-publication-terms-review-20261113 has recorded an answer; the page asserts nothing about them on its own.
context:
Origin: adversarial review of an agent-facing strategy for BenchBox, 2026-11-12. Owner decisions quoted here were made on that date. Line numbers are hints; re-read the cited file before relying on them.

Decision gate: consolidate, do not legislate. Where no policy exists for a question, list it under 'Open questions' in the PR description for the owner and leave it out of the page; never invent a threshold. The owner's review of the PR is the approval gate for content, so open it early as a draft.

Verification rubric: pass only if a reviewer can trace every 'must' or 'should' on the page to a cited source, and the open-questions list is present even if empty.

Consumers: mcp-instructions-carry-methodology-20261112 and end-user-benchmarking-skill-20261112 quote this page and may add no claim it does not contain.

Guardrails: work only in a linked worktree (make worktree-create, then make agent-write-preflight); never edit the primary clone. Related items are delivered together on one feature branch and one PR, as their umbrella item names (site work: BenchBox-dev/benchbox-site); squash-merged. Add a changelog.d fragment for any user-facing change. No live-cloud runs and no credentials in Git or logs. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers) runs only through lock-taking entry points or make heavy-run after make heavy-status. Follow the comment policy (make comment-policy-check). Stop and report instead of widening scope; scope removed during review must be re-homed to a named item or dropped by the owner with a reason.

Revision (2026-11-13), after an independent critique and owner decisions: delivered as its own PR in the site repository after the static result pages, opened as a draft for the owner's review of the content. docs/tpc-licensing-analysis.md covers redistributing TPC tools, not publishing results.

Delivery note (2026-11-13): implementation is delegated to one agent per branch, working in parallel. The planning session is the only tracker writer and one worker can hold one claim, so this item is claimed and finished at closeout, after its PR merges. Work is in progress; do not take it.
description:
Problem: guidance on running a sound benchmark is scattered across the contributing-results page, the understanding-results and comparing-platforms tutorials, the subscale ranking ADR, the README comparability sentence and docs/tpc-licensing-analysis.md. Neither a person nor an agent has one page that says what a run at a given scale and iteration count supports.

Outcome: one page in the benchbox.dev docs that consolidates existing policy. Required sections: what each scale factor supports (smoke, regression, comparison, publication); iterations and warm-up; seed; validation modes and the integrity validator; when two results are comparable (benchmark, scale, phase, tuning mode, execution variant, timing mode, hardware); tuning disclosure; host noise; publication limits (licence terms that restrict publishing benchmark results, the 'Derived from' wording, official against unofficial); how to cite a published result.

Non-goals: no change to ranking policy, validator behaviour or CLI defaults.
